summary: In parallel NFS, metadata and data can be on different servers. When the metadata server restarts, clients may still modify data files, and recovery can lose track of errors a client saw. This document defines how to report errors using LAYOUTRETURN in NFSv4.2.

plainLanguage.summary: A shared storage system has a record keeper and several storage rooms. If the keeper restarts, errors you ran into could be forgotten, so this lets you report them.

questions: how to report errors in pnfs
what is the anonymous stateid in nfs
why does the mds resilver after restart
subtitle: How a pNFS client can tell a restarted metadata server about write errors, so it resilvers only the files that need it.

tldr.problem: When a pNFS metadata server restarts, clients cannot return layouts to report I/O errors on mirrored data files, so the server must assume every unreclaimed file may be inconsistent and resilver it.
tldr.mechanism: The metadata server must accept the anonymous stateid of all zeros in LAYOUTRETURN during the grace period, letting the client report errors with the ff_ioerr4 structure.
tldr.outcome: The server can pick the mirrors without errors and resilver accurately, and it avoids resilvering files that were reclaimed with no errors.

today: RFC 9737 is a Proposed Standard published in February 2025. The unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: The Recovery Gap After a Restart
sections.content:
In Parallel NFS (pNFS) with the flexible file layout (RFC 8435), a file's metadata lives on a metadata server (MDS) and its data lives on data servers (DSs). During recovery after an MDS restart, there is no way for a client to tell the MDS about an error that occurred during a WRITE to the data servers while the MDS was down.

This document is an extension of NFSv4.2 (RFC 7862), built using the process in RFC 8178 on top of the XDR generated from RFC 7863.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a librarian who keeps the catalog and several rooms that hold the books. If the librarian leaves and comes back, there was no way to say 'something went wrong in room two while you were gone.'

sections.title: Why Errors Cannot Be Reported Today
sections.content:
After an MDS restarts, clients get a grace recovery period to recover state they had before. For open files, the client sends an OPEN with a claim type of CLAIM_PREVIOUS, then sends RECLAIM_COMPLETE when it is done reclaiming.

The flexible file layout lets a client mirror files. With client-side mirroring, the client must tell the MDS about I/O errors on a mirror, because that is the only way the MDS can learn a mirror is corrupt and repair it by resilvering. The client normally does this with LAYOUTRETURN and the ff_ioerr4 structure.

The problem is that RFC 8881 requires the client to stop using layouts after a restart, and the layout stateids are no longer valid. LAYOUTRETURN needs a layout stateid, and the client cannot get a layout during grace recovery. So clients have no choice but to not recover files with I/O errors, and the MDS MUST assume the mirrors are inconsistent and pick one for resilvering. Even if the MDS can tell the client modified data during the outage, it MUST NOT assume those modifications were consistent.
sections.plainLanguage: After the keeper comes back, your old library card stops working, so you cannot even walk up to the desk to report the problem. The keeper then assumes the worst and recopies the books.

sections.title: Reporting Errors with the Anonymous Stateid
sections.content:
The fix is that the MDS MUST accept the anonymous stateid of all zeros for the lrf_stateid in LAYOUTRETURN. The client uses it to tell the MDS about errors, and the MDS can then resilver the file accurately by picking the mirrors that have no associated errors.

  • During the grace period, any lrf_stateid other than the all-zeros anonymous stateid gets NFS4ERR_GRACE.
  • After the grace period, an all-zeros lrf_stateid gets NFS4ERR_NO_GRACE.
  • When replying to a LAYOUTRETURN with the anonymous stateid, the MDS MUST NOT bump the seqid of the lorr_stateid.
  • If the returned layout does not match the current mirror instances for the file, the MDS MUST ignore the LAYOUTRETURN and resilver the file.

The MDS MUST also resilver any file that was neither reclaimed with CLAIM_PREVIOUS nor had an error reported, since the client has most likely restarted and lost its state.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of a library card, you can use a special all-zeros pass just to report problems. The keeper takes the pass during the first busy days, then stops taking it afterwards.

sections.title: When to Resilver
sections.content:
A write intent occurs when a client opens a file and gets LAYOUTIOMODE4_RW from the MDS. The MDS MUST track outstanding write intents and, after a restart, track their recovery. How it tracks them is implementation specific.

The decision depends on what the client does before the grace period ends:

  • The client reclaims the file and reports no errors: the MDS MUST NOT resilver it.
  • The client reports an error: the file MUST be resilvered.
  • The client neither reclaims nor reports: under the old behavior, the MDS MUST resilver it.

Resilvering is broadly: fence the file, record the need to resilver, release the write intent, and once there are no write intents on the file, start resilvering. The MDS MUST NOT resilver a file while clients still hold outstanding write intents. It MUST also track the need to resilver, so that if it restarts during the grace period it restarts file recovery on a replayed write intent or starts resilvering on a replayed resilvering intent.

Whether the MDS blocks I/O, forces I/O through itself, or lets a proxy server update the new data file during resilvering is an implementation choice. If the client keeps access, it MUST have the same layout (set of mirror instances) afterwards, and a proxy server MUST stay in the layout until the grace period is finished.
sections.plainLanguage: If you say all is well, the keeper leaves the books alone. If you report a problem, or never show up, the keeper recopies the books from a good room, and waits until everyone has put their pens down first.

sections.title: Version Mismatch
sections.content:
The MDS has no expectations that a client will use this functionality, so if the client does not use it, the MDS functions normally.

If a client does use it and the MDS does not support it, the MDS MUST reply to the LAYOUTRETURN with NFS4ERR_BAD_STATEID. A client that sees this error in this situation should fall back to the old behavior of not reporting errors.
sections.plainLanguage: If the keeper does not know about the special pass, it says no, and you go back to the old way of doing things.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The RFC says there are no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 7862. It also has no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new is risky here beyond what the older rules already cover, and no new registry entries are needed.
